subtitle: Tape Stop and Start
tagline: A tape-style varispeed motor: press PAUSE and the sound slows down and drops in pitch to a stop, press PLAY and it spins back up, along a curve you can draw.

body.lead: TB Tape recreates the sound of a tape machine whose motor is switched off and on. When you pause it, speed and pitch fall together until the tape stops; when you play it again, the tape spins back up to normal speed.

body.p: `STOP TIME` and `START TIME` set how long each transition takes, from instant to two seconds. `MOTOR CURVE` sets how the speed changes along the way, from a straight line to slow, sudden, or stepped changes, or a curve you draw yourself. Because `PLAY` is a host parameter, you can automate tape stops at exact positions in your song.

ul: Varispeed tape stop and spin-up: speed and pitch change together
Independent STOP TIME and START TIME, each from 0 to 2 seconds
MOTOR CURVE with six shapes, freehand drawing, and editable points
Automatable PLAY parameter for exact stops and starts
Reels that show the tape motion live
Bypass that stays aligned with the plug-in's processing latency
8 factory presets, user presets, undo, and redo

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Tape 1.0.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build (AU and VST3) is also version 1.0.0; small differences between platforms are possible.

ol: Insert TB Tape on a track, bus, or the master. The defaults are `STOP TIME` 200 ms, `START TIME` 200 ms, and a LINEAR curve.
Start playback and click `PLAY` / `PAUSE` {{9}}. The tape slows to a stop over STOP TIME; click again and it spins back up over START TIME.
Set `STOP TIME` {{4}} and `START TIME` {{5}} for shorter or longer transitions.
Choose a shape from the curve shape box {{7}}, or draw your own curve {{6}}.
To place stops exactly, automate the Play parameter in your host.

rows: Plays or pauses the tape motor. Pausing slows the tape to a stop over STOP TIME; playing spins it back up over START TIME. Automate the Play parameter to trigger stops at exact song positions.
How long the tape takes to stop (BRAKE). At 0 ms it stops instantly. The knob has an exponential scale, so short times are easier to set.
How long the tape takes to spin back up to normal speed (SPIN-UP).
Bypasses the complete tape-stop effect. TB Tape reports its processing latency to the host, and the bypassed signal stays aligned with it.

body.p: The curve shows how far the speed change has progressed (bottom to top) during a transition (left to right). Its shape decides whether the speed changes evenly, early, late, or in steps.

rows: An even change from start to finish.
Ready-made shapes; choose them from the curve shape box and compare by ear.
Drag across the graph to sketch a curve.
Drag nodes to move them. Double-click empty space to add a node, or double-click a node to delete it.
Shown in the shape box after you edit the curve.

note.text: The curve is not a host parameter. It is saved with the plug-in state and in presets. Curve edits can be undone and redone from the TB TAPE menu.

body.p: Click the TB TAPE title to open the preset menu. It lists the factory presets in the STARTING POINTS and FX groups and your user presets, and offers PREVIOUS PRESET, NEXT PRESET, SAVE USER PRESET..., UNDO, and REDO. Saved presets use the .tbtape extension and include the curve. In the table, a curve exponent of 1.0 is linear; lower values change the speed early, higher values late.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Classic tape stop
recipes.use: The whole mix winds down at the end of a section.
steps: Automate Play to switch off on the last beat before the drop, and on again at the downbeat.

recipes.title: Quick brake
recipes.use: A short, sharp stop on drums or a vocal phrase.
steps: Use it on one track or bus so the rest of the mix keeps playing.

recipes.title: Slow spin-up
recipes.use: A record-like start that rises into pitch.
steps: Switch Play on slightly before the downbeat so the music is up to speed in time.

recipes.title: Late drop
recipes.use: Speed that holds, then falls away at the end.
steps: Edit the curve in POINTS mode to move where the drop begins.

rows: Nothing happens when I press PAUSE.
BYPASS is on, or the host is not playing audio through the track.
Raise STOP TIME, or choose a curve that changes early, such as Early Brake.
Shorten START TIME, or switch Play on earlier.
The curve was edited. Choose a shape from the shape box to replace it.
The curve is not a host parameter. Save different curves as presets, or automate Play, STOP TIME, and START TIME.

First release: a tape-style varispeed motor with independent 0 to 2 second stop and start times; freehand and point-based motor curves with six curve shortcuts; eight factory presets; latency-aligned bypass; a compact 498 × 260 reel-deck interface with live tape-motion feedback.
